2.7.4.2.1.1 Common Adverse Events
Study DPL-301 (NCT05551234), Safety Analysis Set. Gastrointestinal Adverse Reactions
In Trial 1 (NCT05551234), gastrointestinal adverse reactions were reported in 38% of dapralutide-treated patients and 15% of placebo-treated patients; these included nausea (18% vs 5%), diarrhea (9% vs 4%), and vomiting (8% vs 1%). 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience
The safety of cendrolimab was evaluated in CDB-202 (NCT04987654), in which 156 patients with previously treated advanced squamous NSCLC received cendrolimab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks. The median duration of exposure was 5.6 months (range: 0.5 to 21.2).

Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.3% of patients, including pneumonia and sepsis. Grade 3 or 4 adverse reactions occurred in 42% of patients.
Permanent discontinuation of cendrolimab due to an adverse reaction occurred in 9% of patients. Dosage interruptions due to an adverse reaction occurred in 34% of patients.

note: ENGINE TODAY: MISSED TRUE CONFLICT — and it is the brief's own example (612 vs 621). The label's 621 is reported `figure_not_read` ('matched no canonical form'), so the transposition is invisible; the pair's verdict is `no_conflict_among_compared` on the strength of the 1,219 total alone. The label's 621 is framed as arm=total, so it is reported `multiple_values_same_frame` against the ISS total 1,219 and `per_arm_vs_total` against 612 and 607. The label's 541 is `figure_not_read` and the ISS's 514 (84.0%) is left as `no_counterpart` on measure exposure:duration, so the pair reports `no_conflict_among_compared` off the 1,219 total. lu-05 catches this exact 541-vs-514 conflict when the label writes 'Of the dapralutide-treated patients, 541 were exposed for at least 24 weeks'; the natural active-voice variant 'N dapralutide-treated patients were exposed for at least 24 weeks' is not read. 2.7.3.3.2.1 Study DPL-301 (NCT05551234)
In the full analysis set (all randomised patients, N=612; 306 per arm), the proportion of patients reaching HbA1c <7.0% at Week 26 was 51.6% vs 20.9%.

expected.why: 21 vs 20.9. '<7%' / '<7.0%' is the responder threshold, not a rate.

note: ENGINE TODAY: MISSED TRUE CONFLICT. Both label values are `figure_not_read` and the 2.7.3 figures sit as `no_counterpart` on responder:hba1c<7, so verdict is `nothing_compared`. lu-18 reads the same row when its stub is 'Percentage of patients achieving HbA1c <7%'; here the unit is written as a ', %' suffix on the stub, which section 14 tables routinely do, and the row stops being read. Probe G10 shows the same miss with the unit in the table title instead ('(percent of patients)'). A labelled efficacy responder rate that disagrees by 3 percentage points is precisely the section 14 discrepancy that draws an information request.
